records.affected_metric: Any future observed milestone or no-realization summary
records.likely_direction_of_bias: Observed corpus can overrepresent successful progression and undercount adverse paths.
records.mechanism: Successful samples, qualifications, shipments, and launches are more likely to receive official announcements than failed or abandoned efforts.
records.mitigation: Outcome-neutral Track registry, completed adverse search, explicit negative threshold, and no inference from silence.
records.residual_limitation: Disclosure remains Missing Not At Random; unannounced failures are not recoverable.

records.likely_direction_of_bias: Technical acceptance can appear more complete and failures less frequent than reality.
records.mechanism: Named qualification completion, failure criteria, and rejected samples are usually confidential.
records.mitigation: Keep substages literal and require explicit product-scope negative evidence.
records.residual_limitation: The corpus cannot identify a full qualification denominator.

records.affected_metric: Commitment, O1 scope, and decision translation
records.likely_direction_of_bias: Commercial selection is missing and broad supplier claims can be overgeneralized.
records.mechanism: Customer identity, contract, allocation, price, volume, and supplier share are often private.
records.mitigation: Preserve KNOWN_UNKNOWN fields and prohibit inferred customer/supplier bridges.
records.residual_limitation: Public O1 is only a supplier-side commercialization proxy.

records.likely_direction_of_bias: Disclosure-heavy suppliers can appear to progress through more observable stages.
records.mechanism: Suppliers use different milestone verbs, cadence, and product/customer scope.
records.mitigation: Literal stage taxonomy, leave-one-supplier sensitivity if later authorized, and no imputation.
records.residual_limitation: Comparability remains limited even after deterministic normalization.

records.likely_direction_of_bias: H1-C can look more complete for disclosure-structure reasons, not superior signal quality.
records.mechanism: Cloud providers publish named service availability more systematically than memory suppliers publish commercial selection.
records.mitigation: Never pool strata or compare raw coverage as performance.
records.residual_limitation: Cross-strata data completeness remains structurally different.

records.affected_metric: Any future count or comparison using CAPEX
records.likely_direction_of_bias: Repeated references can create pseudo-replication and false independence.
records.mechanism: One company-period CAPEX disclosure is referenced by several named Platform Tracks.
records.mitigation: Count independence by origin group and permit Track reuse as context only.
records.residual_limitation: CAPEX remains broad and cannot be allocated to a named SKU.

records.affected_metric: Any future no-realization or timing description
records.likely_direction_of_bias: Recent Tracks can be incorrectly treated as failures or omitted in a way that favors older successes.
records.mechanism: HBM4/HBM4E and Blackwell Tracks have less elapsed follow-up than older generations.
records.mitigation: Frozen 6/12/18-month readiness flags and denominator exclusion for right-censored Events.
records.residual_limitation: Longer follow-up is not available at this Gate 6 cutoff.

records.likely_direction_of_bias: Availability can be mistaken for high use or realized memory volume.
records.mechanism: GA or installed infrastructure is publicly visible while utilization and memory consumption are usually not.
records.mitigation: Keep GA, limited availability, installed, and operational subtypes separate.
records.residual_limitation: Public sources do not establish actual utilization or exact HBM demand.
